---
title: "Output Formats"
---

Gridwell renders the table IR to 11 output formats, split into text (returns a string) and
binary (returns bytes). Which styling features each Tier-1 writer (HTML, LaTeX, Typst,
RTF, DOCX, XLSX) actually expresses is measured, not claimed: see the
[Feature Matrix](feature-matrix.qmd).

## Text Formats

### HTML

- Semantic HTML5 with `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`
- A fragment for a host page, not a styled document: the `<style>` block holds only what
  the table's styles define (and cell alignment), so fonts, rules and padding come from
  the page. Opened on its own, an unstyled table looks plain.
- Scoped `<style>` block with generated class names
- Optional inline-style mode for email/embedded contexts
- Footnote marks as `<sup>` linked to footer
- Accessibility: `scope`, `aria-label`, `<caption>`

### LaTeX

- Uses `booktabs` (`\toprule`, `\midrule`, `\bottomrule`); a column spanner is underlined
  with `\cmidrule` over its columns (`\cline` without booktabs)
- `\multicolumn` and `\multirow` for spans
- Column alignment via `l`, `r`, `c`, `p{width}`
- Cell fills via `\cellcolor`, text color via `\textcolor`; underline and strike-through via
  `\uline` / `\sout`; sizes via `\fontsize`
- Required packages: `booktabs`, `multirow`, `longtable` (long tables), `xcolor` with the
  `table` option, and `ulem` with `normalem` (`\usepackage[normalem]{ulem}`, so `\emph`
  keeps its meaning)
- Special characters escaped: `& % $ # _ { } ~ ^ \`

### Typst

- Uses Typst's `#table()` function with named parameters
- `table.cell(colspan: N, rowspan: N)` for spans
- Column widths mapped to Typst length values
- Styles via `table.cell(fill: ...)`, `text(weight: "bold")`

### RTF

- Full RTF document with color and font tables
- Column spans via `\cellx` boundaries, row spans via `\clvmgf`/`\clvmrg`
- Column widths in twips (1/1440 inch)
- Cell fills via `\clcbpat`; no per-cell borders yet

### SVG

- Standalone SVG image with embedded text
- Text as `<text>` elements with computed positions
- Backgrounds as `<rect>`, borders as `<line>` strokes
- Self-contained (no external dependencies)

### ANSI (Terminal)

- Box-drawing characters for borders (Unicode); rules run unbroken over and under cells
  that span columns
- Footnote marks as Unicode superscripts, in cells and in the notes below
- 24-bit ANSI color sequences
- Column widths computed from content
- Text truncation with ellipsis for overflow
- Saved to a file (`.txt`), it is plain text with no escape codes unless the `color`
  option is set

### Pandoc

- Pandoc JSON AST format (`Table` constructor)
- Supports all inline formatting (Strong, Emph, Superscript, etc.)
- Usable with `pandoc -f json -t docx/pdf/epub/...`

### Quarto

- The Pandoc JSON AST, as for the Pandoc format, for Quarto's Pandoc-based pipeline
- Optionally wrapped in a `tbl-<id>` div for cross-references (`table_id` option)

## Binary Formats

### DOCX (Microsoft Word)

- Valid Office Open XML archive (ZIP)
- Table in `word/document.xml`
- Horizontal merge via `<w:gridSpan>`, vertical via `<w:vMerge>`
- Bold, italic, color, shading and alignment; table-wide single borders (per-cell borders,
  font size and family are not written yet)

### XLSX (Microsoft Excel)

- SpreadsheetML format
- Cells preserve typed values (numbers stay numeric), with a number format that shows them
  as the table does (`0.0` for `76.0`, `#,##0` for `1,250`). A typed cell whose display
  is not a plain number (`<0.001`, a footnote mark) stays text.
- Merge regions via `<mergeCells>`
- Styles in `xl/styles.xml` (fonts, fills, borders, number formats); rich text where a
  cell mixes formatting, in the shared-string table (apps such as Numbers ignore run
  formatting in inline strings)
- Cells with line breaks wrap, and rows are tall enough for their lines and font sizes

### PPTX (Microsoft PowerPoint)

- DrawingML table (`<a:tbl>`) in a slide shape
- Grid-based spans with `gridSpan`/`rowSpan` attributes
- Text color, weight, slant and size, cell fills and alignment
- A complete package (theme, master color map, notes size), so PowerPoint and Keynote
  open it
